profile.entities: Sula Vineyards Ltd; The Haven by Sula; Domaine Sula; Chandon Estate (Pending Acquisition)
profile.themes: Wine Tourism scaling as primary growth engine; Grape mix cost headwinds; CSD expansion; EU FTA duty reduction prep

bull_bear.body: Deleveraging priority (Net debt down to INR 280cr). Final dividend INR 2/share declared. M&A focused on tourism assets (Chandon) and potential craft spirit brands. No buyback mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Grape mix cost overhang persisting until next harvest (Q3FY27). EU FTA duty reduction (1 year out) threatening premium segment pricing power. Summer heat damaging retail inventory (lack of AC in trade). Unsustainable discounting by competitors in economy segment.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic. Acknowledges margin pain as temporary/structural shift for quality. Aggressive on Tourism scaling ('laser focused'). Disciplined on M&A (waiting for right fit in spirits). Transparent on cost headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'margin compression' is partly a quality upgrade story (using premium grapes in entry-level wines) which may boost long-term brand equity despite short-term P&L hit. Tourism revenue reported ex-wine sales in P&L, understating the true INR 110cr scale of the vertical. 75% renewable energy mix achieved; moving to battery storage to hedge power costs.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Healthy Balance Sheet with Debt-to-EBITDA at <3x (FY26)".
- Capital discipline framed through price paid and capex efficiency: the Domaine Rāsā estate acquired at "a highly attractive price of INR 20 crore", and 1 Mn litres of cellar capacity added in FY26 "at 33% lower capex".
- Working capital is an explicit constraint shaping operations — the shift to a higher mix of wine grapes versus table grapes is described as "aimed at conserving working capital", at the cost of ~150 bps of gross margin.
- Stated ambition: "Accelerating Earnings Growth over next 3 years (FY26-FY29) with improved EBITDA margins and capital efficiency".
- Long-run track record cited: "Delivered Revenue, Operating EBITDA and PAT CAGR of 6%, 11% and 52% over FY21-26"; the deck makes no mention of dividend policy or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Own Brands: +5% YoY in Q4; Elite/Premium mix at 79% of sales. The Source range +35% in Q4, now >10% of own brands. Wine Tourism: +17% revenue in Q4, +20% full year; Crossed INR 100cr annual run-rate (INR 110cr incl. wine sold onsite). Footfalls >4 lakh. Occupancy >70% (core resorts >80%).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grape surplus forcing use of premium grapes in economy wines; margin pressure | Indian Wine Consumers | beneficiary | High | Getting higher quality wine (Chenin Blanc/Shiraz) in economy labels at same price points. |
| EU FTA duty reduction looming; premium pricing power at risk | Small Domestic Premium Winemakers | loser | Med | Sula's scale and brand premium allow it to compete; smaller players may face margin squeeze or consolidation. |
| Hospitality capacity constraints limiting high-margin revenue | Sula Vineyards Limited | beneficiary | High | Aggressive capex into tourism (3x winery spend) and Chandon acquisition directly address this bottleneck. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Market leader with >50% share in domestic premium wines"; Sula's Shiraz Cabernet is described as "India's highest selling wine".
- Winery capacity of 19.2 Mn litres, stated to be "amongst top 5 in Asia"; ~2,600 acres of contracted vineyards, "higher than next two Indian wine producers combined".
- Wide and diverse portfolio of 60+ labels across 14 brands and across price points and grape varietals; "Sula has won 50+ Awards over the last decade".
- Wine tourism assets described as "Among world's most visited vineyards with 400K+ visitors* in FY26" (*including resorts); the flagship tasting room and bottle shop near The Source is "among the most visited globally recording 3+ lakh visitors in FY26".
- Wine Tourism contribution to total revenue up 120 bps YoY to 13% in Q1FY27.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Completion of the Chandon Estate purchase in Q1 FY27 and its rebranding to Domaine Rāsā is the deck's headline corporate event, opening the presentation ahead of performance highlights.
- [Geographic mix] Telangana, Haryana, Chandigarh, CSD and Exports delivered strong double-digit growth, while "Karnataka continues to remain soft; expect it to turn a corner in H2 FY27" — and the shortfall in core markets (Maharashtra & Karnataka) is named as a driver of adverse market mix on gross margin.
- [Multi-year trajectory] The FY21-FY26 revenue-from-operations series printed is 418 / 454 / 553 / 609 / 619 / 596 (INR Cr) with a stated 6% CAGR, i.e. FY26 revenue was below FY25; Operating EBITDA over the same span was 61 / 113 / 158 / 176 / 149 / 103 (INR Cr) at margins of 14.6% / 25.0% / 28.5% / 28.9% / 24.1% / 17.3%, and PAT was 3 / 52 / 84 / 93 / 70 / 26 (INR Cr). The FY26 figures show a marked step-down from the FY24 peak.
- [Wine tourism trajectory] Wine tourism revenue series of 18 / 35 / 45 / 55 / 60 / 73 (INR Cr) for FY21-FY26, a stated 32% CAGR — the fastest-growing disclosed line and the only one of the six charted series rising in FY26.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin pressured by 350-400bps (expensive wine grapes used in economy labels due to surplus) + 150bps (prior year one-off). Packing material costs rising (West Asia conflict); Price hikes of 2-3% planned in free-pricing states. Opex reduced 3% YoY via cost controls.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: Momentum carrying into FY27 (4 months straight growth); Wine Tourism to grow double-digits as 'The Haven' scales. Margins: Expect improvement post-Q3FY27 as grape mix impact normalizes; Opex controls ongoing. Order Inflow: N/A. Capex: FY27 regular capex < FY26 (INR 25cr); Heavy skew toward Tourism (3x winery capex); Chandon acquisition closing H1FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - FMCG inventory model. Channel inventory destocked in Q4 vs prior quarters. WIPS receivables at INR 81cr (controlled).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Chandon Estate (19 acres) acquisition pending; Targeting >200 room keys within 1.5 years (vs current 154). New event pavilion (Q3FY27) and amphitheater expansion (Q2FY27). CSD listings expanding from 9 to 14 wines by Q4FY27. Potential entry into spirits/tequila via M&A (no target yet).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sula returned to top-line growth in Q4 (+7% YoY) driven by Wine Tourism (+17%) and elite brand recovery, though margins compressed due to a strategic shift to costlier wine grapes and a prior-year one-off gain. The strategic pivot toward high-margin hospitality (targeting >20% revenue mix) and the pending Chandon estate acquisition signal a structural re-rating from a pure-play winemaker to an integrated experiential luxury operator.
